diseases.name: Apple Mosaic
diseases.description: A virus disease of apple that marks the leaves with pale yellow to cream patches and bands.
diseases.causes: The virus is carried in the tree's sap and spreads through grafting and budding with infected wood; no insect spreads it.
symptoms: Pale yellow to cream spots, blotches or bands, often along the veins
Some leaves scorch and drop in hot weather
diseases.effect: Infected trees grow and crop somewhat less; the marks do not spread to healthy trees in the orchard.
diseases.untreated: The tree stays infected for life; yields of sensitive varieties fall over the years.

steps.title: Confirm the pattern
steps.instruction: Compare the marks with reference photos and ask for a lab test if unsure.
steps.rationale: Nutrient problems and sprays can cause similar marks.

steps.title: Do not propagate from it
steps.instruction: Never take budwood or grafts from this tree.
steps.rationale: Grafting is how the virus spreads.

steps.title: Replace badly affected young trees
steps.instruction: Remove young trees that are heavily marked and slow-growing, and replant with certified stock.
steps.rationale: There is no cure; a healthy tree recovers the yield.

prevention.title: Plant certified virus-tested trees
prevention.detail: Clean nursery stock is the only real control.

lifecycle: The virus lives in the tree's sap.
It passes to new trees through grafted buds and rootstocks.
Spring leaves show cream spots and vein bands.
Every tree grafted from it is infected too.
